newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity called higher on outage rumours.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity called higher on outage rumours.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open higher Wednesday on market rumors that a unit the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant tripped off line early today, market sources said.

In over-the-counter activity, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were quoted $33.60-34.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), up from Tuesday's settlement at $33.54, and August California-Oregon Border (COB) was talked $22.90-23.10 at $22.93 firmer than yesterday's close at $22.93.
"Everyone pulled their offers," a Houston futures trader said, referring to a disappearance of sellers in over-the-counter activity when the rumors of a Diablo Canyon outage became widely circulated.
The 1,070 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon unit 2, in Avila Beach on the central California coast was said to be taken offline to repair a problem in the feedwater system.
Diablo Canyon 2 was running at 100 percent power early Wednesday, according to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's (NRC) daily plant status report.
Southern California Edison Co's 1,070 MW San Onofre unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
San Onofre 2 was shut Sunday to replace its charge line check valves, and San Onofre has been out of service since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.

Meteorologist called for a warming trend to begin later this week in the Pacific Northwest following recent cooler-than-normal weather across the region. Meanwhile, they expect temperatures in the Southwest to stay near to above normal through next week.
